subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should Copilot Claude `anthropic-messages` silent aborts fail fast, trigger model fallback only when replay-safe, or remain strict errors after the cron status fix?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses provider routing and model fallback policy, and allowing fallback after an abort can replay side-effectful agent work unless maintainers define the safe boundary.

options.title: Fail fast plus replay-safe fallback
options.body: Add a provider/runtime timeout or progress signal and allow fallback only when the run has no delivery or side-effect evidence; keep aborted runs as cron errors otherwise.

options.title: Strict error after abort
options.body: Keep aborted Copilot runs out of fallback and rely on the existing cron error classification plus clearer operator diagnostics.

options.title: Default fallback seeding only
options.body: Revive the narrower Copilot fallback-default direction, accepting that it does not by itself fix silent `anthropic-messages` streams that never reach a fallback-safe failure.

recommendation.title: Fail fast plus replay-safe fallback
recommendation.body: Add a provider/runtime timeout or progress signal and allow fallback only when the run has no delivery or side-effect evidence; keep aborted runs as cron errors otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is centered on the GitHub Copilot provider and Copilot Claude stream/fallback policy, where this history is strongest.
